About

Who I am and where I’ve worked.

I’m a Customer Support and Virtual Assistance professional with five years of experience spanning customer communication, appointment setting, CRM management, administrative support, teaching and project coordination.

I bring a combination of people skills, organisation and problem-solving to help businesses deliver better customer experiences and keep daily operations running smoothly.

I started in hospitality in 2021 as a Hotel Supervisor at Oxbow Lake Hotel, an onsite role where I ran daily operations, trained new staff and handled guest concerns face to face. In 2022 I taught and guided over 250 students as a secondary school teacher during my NYSC year. In 2024 I moved into remote support at Float, working with US-based customers across phone calls, live chat and email.

Across hospitality, teaching and remote support, the approach has stayed the same: listen carefully, take ownership of the issue and follow it through to a clear outcome. With five years in customer support, appointment setting, CRM management, administrative support and project coordination, I bring patience, organisation and dependable follow-through. For a business, that means customers who feel heard, records that stay accurate and daily operations that run smoothly.

Expertise

What I can do for your team.

Support & issue resolution

Responding to customer enquiries with clear, accurate information, resolving issues where possible and ensuring complex cases are properly escalated and followed up.

Communication & follow-up

Writing replies that say what happens next, checking back to confirm the issue is resolved and keeping customers updated until the ticket is closed.

Inbound & outbound calls

Handling calls with customers and prospects, including international callers: answering questions, explaining next steps and logging each conversation afterwards.

Appointment setting

Finding out what a prospect needs, booking the appointment in the calendar and passing the lead to sales with notes, so the call starts informed.

CRM & customer records

Creating and updating contact details, ticket history and status in tools like Zendesk and HubSpot, so the next person can pick up any case without asking the customer to repeat themselves.

Lead follow-up & sales support

Tracking each lead by status (New, Contacted, Follow-up, Closed), recording follow-up dates and flagging open items, so interested prospects are not forgotten.

Administrative support

Managing inboxes, calendars and documents, preparing weekly reports and setting up booking pages and automations in Google Calendar, Gmail and Zapier.

Team coordination & projects

Assigning tasks, tracking deadlines and updating progress in Trello, Asana and ClickUp, and keeping project documentation current.

Case studies

Problems I Solved, Results I Delivered

A look at how I handle customers, teams and schedules, and the outcomes that followed.

Float · Customer support

The customer who writes twice is the one you didn’t help the first time

An unanswered issue never stays small. It becomes a second email, a sharper tone and a customer quietly deciding whether you’re worth the trouble.

The challenge
Customers contacted support with account and service issues, and each one needed a correct answer and a full resolution, not a holding reply. Every case had to be handled, tracked and escalated cleanly so no customer had to repeat themselves.
My role
Customer Support Specialist: first contact, investigator and owner of the issue until it was closed or properly handed over.
What I did
  • Read every request closely and checked the facts before answering, so replies were specific instead of generic.
  • Gave each customer the answer and the next step in the same message.
  • Escalated complex cases with the full history, so the next person never had to ask the customer to start again.
  • Logged each interaction in Zendesk and followed up to confirm the issue was resolved.
Result
Every interaction was logged in Zendesk with its history attached, and complex cases were escalated with the full record, so no customer had to explain their issue twice.
Float · Appointment setting

A good call ends with a time in the calendar

“We’ll be in touch” is how interested people go cold. A conversation only creates value when the next step has a date on it.

The challenge
Prospects needed to be reached, understood and booked into the calendar, with accurate records and clear notes, so the sales team could pick up each lead without re-qualifying them.
My role
Appointment Setter: calls, lead follow-up, scheduling and record keeping.
What I did
  • Handled inbound and outbound calls and found out what each prospect actually needed.
  • Followed up with leads instead of waiting for them to return.
  • Scheduled appointments and kept CRM records accurate.
  • Passed qualified leads on with the context the next person needed.
Result
Calls ended in booked appointments, CRM records were updated after every call, and qualified leads reached the team with notes, so nobody had to re-qualify them.
Oxbow Lake Hotel · Operations

Guests never see the rota. They feel whether it worked.

Behind every smooth check-in is a team that was briefed, trained and kept in sync. When that slips, the guest is the first to notice.

The challenge
Keeping service standards consistent across every shift while managing a team and resolving guest concerns on the spot, before they could turn into bigger problems.
My role
Hotel Supervisor: the person staff turned to for direction and guests turned to when something went wrong.
What I did
  • Assigned duties and kept an eye on how they were carried out.
  • Trained new employees so standards didn’t depend on who was on shift.
  • Dealt with complaints directly and fixed service issues quickly.
  • Kept communication moving between team members and watched service quality across the day.
Result
Over 90% guest satisfaction maintained while supervising the team, with new staff trained to the same standard and guest complaints handled on the spot.
Itam Secondary School · Teaching (NYSC)

A classroom only works when every student is brought along

Students who fall behind rarely say so. They go quiet. Good teaching is noticing that early and doing something about it.

The challenge
Over 250 students at different levels needed lessons they could follow, progress that was assessed fairly and help when they struggled. With a group that size, a student who was quietly falling behind was easy to miss, and the gap only grew the longer it went unnoticed.
My role
Secondary School Teacher (NYSC): planned and delivered lessons, ran the classroom and supported students one to one.
What I did
  • Planned lessons and delivered them so students could follow.
  • Assessed progress to see who understood the work and who needed more help.
  • Ran the classroom day to day and kept lessons orderly.
  • Gave one-to-one guidance to students who needed it.
Result
250+ students taught and guided, with progress assessed and one-to-one support given to the students who needed it.
Project coordination

Projects stay on track when everyone can see where they stand

Work slips when nobody can see it. A task board, a deadline and an updated document turn a loose plan into something a client can trust.

The challenge
Projects involved many tasks, deadlines and documents moving at the same time. Without clear ownership and tracking, deadlines slip quietly, clients are left guessing where things stand and small delays turn into missed deliveries.
My role
Project coordination and management: organising tasks, tracking deadlines and keeping progress visible.
What I did
  • Organised project work into tasks and assigned them with clear due dates.
  • Tracked deadlines and monitored progress as tasks moved through each stage.
  • Updated progress so the team and client could see where each project stood.
  • Kept project documentation up to date.
Result
95% of projects completed with client satisfaction.
